parameters.content:
# Create step-by-step guides from YouTube tutorials with Apify and OpenAI

## Who's it for

Technical writers, support teams and course creators who would rather skim a written guide than scrub through a video tutorial.

## How it works

1. A form takes a public YouTube URL and an optional start, end and step interval.
2. An HTTP Request node runs the Frameskim actor on Apify, which returns a screenshot, its timestamp and the spoken words for each step.
3. OpenAI writes a short title and one instruction per step, using only the transcript.
4. A Code node builds a Markdown guide with a screenshot and a video link per step; the form's last page downloads it as `guide.md`.

## How to set up

1. Copy your Apify API token from Settings > API & Integrations.
2. In **Run Frameskim on Apify**, create a Header Auth credential: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer <your token>`.
3. Add your OpenAI credential in **OpenAI model for step text**.
4. Open the form and submit a tutorial URL.

## Requirements

- An Apify account. Frameskim costs about $0.12 per video plus $0.015 per frame, capped at $1 per run.
- An OpenAI API key.
- A public video with captions.

If YouTube blocks the video download, Frameskim falls back to YouTube's storyboard images: low resolution screenshots at $0.002 each.

## How to customize

Edit **Configure guide settings** to change the step interval, frame limit, caption language, cost cap or OpenAI model. Swap OpenAI for any chat model, or send the Markdown to Notion, Google Docs or email.

## 1. Input and settings
The form asks for the YouTube URL and an optional start, end and interval. **Configure guide settings** holds every value you may want to change: `intervalSeconds` (used when the form leaves the interval empty), `maxFrames`, `language` (caption language), `maxChargeUsd` (cost cap per run) and `openaiModel`.

## 2. Run Frameskim on Apify
Calls the Apify actor `emttn/frameskim` in `segment` mode:
`POST https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/emttn~frameskim/run-sync-get-dataset-items`

Credential: **Header Auth**, name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_APIFY_TOKEN`. It is stored in n8n, never in the workflow. The `maxTotalChargeUsd` query parameter caps what a run can cost.

Apify waits up to 300 s for a synchronous run and then answers 408. Frameskim stops itself before that limit; if you ever get a 408, narrow the start and end range.

## 3. Write each step
One LLM call per frame turns the words spoken there into a short title and one instruction, without inventing details. Replace the OpenAI model with Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama or any other chat model sub-node.

## 4. Build the guide and return it
The Code node pairs each answer with its screenshot and a link to that second of the video, and **Save guide as Markdown file** turns it into `guide.md`. **Return guide to the form** is the form's last page: it shows a short message and downloads the file in the browser of whoever filled the form. The Markdown is also in the `markdown` field, ready for Notion, Google Docs or email.

Screenshot links point to your Apify storage and expire with your plan's data retention; download the images to keep the guide long term.
